summary: Iteration 2: tested forgot/reset password, forgot-password rate limit, admin change-own-password (restored to original), learner blocked from /admin/password, admin lesson reorder (lesson-05 -> 2 -> 5), admin Yes/Maybe/Not yet reflection column, and regression of login/dashboard/lesson completion. Backend 18/18 pytest pass. All UI flows work. One frontend race bug found in AdminLessonEdit (double fetch under React StrictMode overwrites quick edits). Admin password confirmed back to z-lQI9UdjCj48kvM; lesson order confirmed back to 1..14 (lesson-01..lesson-14).

minor.issue: Existing JWTs (7-day) are still valid after a password reset or change. Other sessions are not signed out, so a stolen session survives a reset. Suggestion: store a password_changed_at/token_version on the user and check it in current_user.
If the user behind a valid token has been deleted, find_one returns None and user['_id'] raises a 500. Return 400 instead.

The email is sent inline, so known emails take noticeably longer to answer than unknown ones. This timing difference lets someone check which emails have accounts. Consider sending in a BackgroundTask. Email currently fails with 402 insufficient_credits (expected): the 503 HTTPException is caught and logged, and the generic 200 is still returned (verified in the backend.err.log).

backend/.env FRONTEND_URL (1269118e-...preview.emergentagent.com) differs from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (ai-in--6775ra7d...). It responds, but reset links in emails will point to that host. Confirm it is the intended public domain for production.

ui_bugs.issue: Race condition: under React.StrictMode the useEffect fetches GET /lessons/:id twice (confirmed: 2 GETs per page load). The second response calls setF and overwrites any edits made before it arrives. In automation, filling order=2 right after the form appeared sent the stale order in the PUT, so the lesson did not move. With a 2s wait it works correctly. Real users editing very quickly, or on a slow network, could lose edits. Fix: use an ignore/abort flag in the effect cleanup, or only setF when f is null.

action_items: Fix AdminLessonEdit fetch race (ignore stale/duplicate response in useEffect cleanup) so edits are not overwritten
Invalidate existing sessions after password reset/change (token_version)
Guard reset_password against a deleted user (return 400, not 500)
Optional: send the reset email in a background task to remove the timing difference that reveals which emails have accounts
Confirm FRONTEND_URL is the correct public domain for reset links
critical_code_review_comments: admin_update_lesson renumbers with N sequential update_one calls, not atomically. Two admins saving at once could leave duplicate orders. Acceptable for a single-admin MVP; bulk_write would be cleaner.
Rate limit counts tokens by created_at only, which is correct. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes, and all of a user's tokens are invalidated on use. Good.
pytest.ini enables xdist (-n). The iteration-2 test file has order-dependent tests sharing a module fixture, so run it with -n 0.

rca of the issue: AdminLessonEdit: useEffect([id]) -> api.get().then(setF) has no cleanup. React 18 StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts in dev, so two requests run, and the later-resolving one replaces user edits. Reproduced: fill order=5 right after load -> the PUT body had order:2 (stale). Mitigation: let cancelled = false; return () => { cancelled = true } and skip setF when cancelled.
